result.title: From Activity Recognition to Shift Detection: Variational Wi-Fi Sensing with Evidential Uncertainty
result.summary: Human motion perturbs wireless channels, making commodity Wi-Fi devices a practical platform for device-free activity recognition. Yet Channel State Information (CSI) also depends strongly on the person, receiver position, recording session, and surrounding environment, so a classifier can continue producing activity labels after its deployment conditions have moved away from those seen during training. We propose Wi-HAR, a multi-antenna architecture in which four Variational Auto-Encoders learn compact distributions from raw Wi-Fi 6 CSI magnitudes and a delayed-fusion classifier combines their means and log-variances. On twelve activities from a public benchmark, Wi-HAR reaches 96.6% median recognition accuracy, compared with 70.8-81.5% for independently optimized single-antenna models, showing that the antennas provide complementary views of the same activity. We then use the same latent backbone to detect deployment shifts without using shifted samples for model selection or calibration. A class-conditional uncertainty score derived from Evidential Deep Learning achieves a macro-average ROC-AUC of 0.897 across eleven datasets that change receiver position, participant, recording session, or room, and detects 82.5% of shifted samples at a realized 5.2% in-distribution rejection rate. Detection performance nevertheless varies substantially across receiver positions, showing that the same physical change does not induce a uniform uncertainty response. The compact representation also supports shallow decision-tree analysis using variables from several antennas.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Wi-HAR：用四个 VAE 从 Wi-Fi 6 CSI 幅度中学习紧凑分布，延迟融合各天线的均值与对数方差完成活动识别，并复用同一 latent 骨干，以 Evidential Deep Learning 导出的类别条件不确定性分数检测部署条件漂移。
AI.relevance_reason: 从 latent 分布的方差与证据不确定性直接导出漂移/拒绝判据、且不使用漂移样本做校准，这一做法可能可供核查 LVR 中「何时停止推理或不信任当前 latent 状态」的决策信号设计；但模态与应用差距大，属远距离借鉴线索。
